criteria.requirement: Repair LCSSeq and LCSStr preparation/reconstruction for qval=None words, qval>1 qgrams and qval=1 ordinary str/list/tuple inputs. Prepare exactly once; recursive multi-input LCSSeq must not retokenize prepared units. Strings at qval=1 retain str results; words/qgrams return lists of original units; ordinary list/tuple preserve first-input representation and unhashable tokens work. Empty/single/multi-input and the 200-element branch boundary follow the same contract. similarity and normalized maximum count prepared units, never concatenated character lengths. Preserve the previously delivered custom-predicate LCSSeq behavior and old character results/tie rules. This is one complete sequence-unit repair across both algorithms, not separate micro-goals for each branch.

Investigate the real source, explain the call path and clarify the business requirements before obtaining plan approval and implementing. Deliver real engineering changes, public regression tests that fail on the original version, and English compatibility documentation. Repair independently reported failures; questions, answers and documentation do not count as separate completed objectives.

comparison: Accept equivalent implementations according to actual business behavior and the frozen scope; do not grade by matching the reference patch text.
